scope: Owner-requested evaluation of the Boxer phone/tablet contact engine (playing it repeatedly, analysing timing, rhythm and flow, and stress-testing the glove collision engine), followed by a written Codex work order for Editions 1-2 and the engine foundation, a roadmap for later editions, and the numbers-only harness that produced every figure. It opens MA-OPERA-015, records eleven owner decisions and adds cross-references. It benefits the child by making guard teachable: guards and finger lifts stop reading as mistakes, help stops maxing out on one slip, direction starts to matter, slow hands get time to counter, and purposeful play becomes faster than scribbling. No game script, scene, asset, audio, save key or workflow is changed, and no image is made.

acceptance_gaps: Nothing in the game is implemented. Work packages BX0-BX9 and acceptance AC-1 to AC-10 remain open, including device (Lenovo Tab M11 and a phone), observed-child and owner review of the warning's look and the hooks' feel. The playthrough figures come from child timing models built from published averages, not from the intended child. No visual claim is made: no screenshots were taken.

lessons.lesson: A crossing harness that delivers a frame's input after _process lags the glove one frame and reported misses up to 118 px that were the harness's own error; Godot delivers a frame's input first and then advances time to the same moment.
When a surface and its host both react to the same zero-amount gesture by raising help, one slip counts twice; give help a single owner.
A random-input bot is a cheap check of DL-AGE-05: it exposed that Title Imp rewards scribbling as much as trying, which no existing probe measured.
